names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 26 aprilie, «Sfânta Cuvioasă Glafira».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Απριλίου, «Αγία Γλαφυρή», with the rank word left off; the page's couplet and the page for Basileus write the name Γλαφύρα.

Read out of the body of the Охридски пролог's entry for 26. април ст. ст., „девицу Глафиру“ and „умре Глафира“ — the heading names only the bishop, so there is no heading form to take. The accusative девицу Глафиру is restored to the nominative the second mention prints, and девица is the `virgin` this folder already carries in `types`. The body gives her no epithet, no family and no city, so the bare forename is the whole of the Serbian form; Italy, which doxologia gives her, is nowhere on this page.

The name link behind the day’s line is page 2443, titled «Глафира Амасийская, дева», with the rank word «дева» stripped per BRIEF.md §4. THE EPITHET IS THE NAME PAGE’S AND NOT THE LINE’S: the day prints only «Прав. Глафиры девы», a bare forename, and «Амасийская» — of Amasea, the city she fled to and where she died — comes from the link behind it, which is where §3 says the calendar’s own nominative is to be read. Measured against the gate’s own key function before it was written: 'амасииская глафира' has no other holder.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 26 апреля ст. ст. — «Прав. Глафиры девы (322).»

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. THE FOLDER’S FIRST `dates` OF ANY KIND: the line heads her «(322)» and the life says «Праведная Глафира скончалась (+ 322), прежде чем приказ дошел до Амасии» — she died before the emperor’s order reached Amasea. Only the year was written and no narrower claim. `types_add: righteous`, read off the line’s «Прав.», праведная, which is the grade this calendar gives her where the Romanian and the Greek grade her venerable and virgin; the existing `venerable` and `virgin` stand and nothing was removed. THE LIFE IS THE SAME PAGE AS `basileus-of-amasea`’s, life936, titled for the two of them together, which is why the day links it twice. What it turns differently from the three accounts the folder already has: Licinius’s wife is named «Констанция» and it is SHE who dressed Glaphyra in man’s clothing, gave her money and sent her out of the city with trusted servants, putting it about that the maidservant had gone mad and lay dying; Glaphyra gave the whole of that money to the building of the bishop’s church and wrote to the empress for more, which was sent; and it is HER OWN LETTER that fell into the emperor’s hands, not a eunuch’s interception of the reply. The day page prints five hymns and NONE under her name. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 26 aprilie — «Sfânta Cuvioasă Glafira»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Απριλίου — «Αγία Γλαφυρή»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps her, and it is plainly the same woman: the maidservant of Constantia the wife of Licinius, sent away from Licinius's designs by the empress herself, a wanderer in the East, and at last at Amasea with the bishop Basileus, to whom she gave her money for the building of a church, and where she died in peace. **What the Greek puts differently is who sent her away and what she carried.** Here it is the empress who removes her «αφού την εφοδίασε με πολλά χρήματα», having furnished her with a great deal of money, and Glaphyra's own money is what builds the church; the flight in men's clothes, which the Romanian life has, is on saint.gr's page for Basileus rather than on hers, and that page also says she was already dead before Licinius could reach her. It parenthesizes the bishop's own feast, «στον επίσκοπο της πόλης αυτής Βασιλέα (εορτάζει στις 26 Απριλίου)». It gives no year, so this folder's empty `dates` were left empty. It prints no hymn and names no relic.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 09.05.2026 (26. април ст. ст.) — „Свешт. муч. Василије еп. Амасијски.“

attestations.note: **The heading names the bishop of Amasea alone and the body is where this book puts her**, so the citation above is that heading whole, per BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4, and this row is written on the ruling the coordinator gave for a heading that names one man while the body names more. The body's own words are „При нападу ове нечисте страсти он хтеде оскврнити девицу Глафиру, која стајаше у служби царичиној“ and, at the end, „У међувремену умре Глафира“. **This is an extension of that ruling and is flagged as one**: Glaphyra is not an enumerated companion in the martyrdom but a person whose story this entry tells at length, and whom the corpus already keeps on this same menologion day under the Romanian and the Greek. Refusing the row would lose a saint the source names on the day it names her; the author can revert it in one commit. **The entry gives her no year** — she dies „у међувремену“, before the order reached the governor — so this folder's empty `dates` were left empty, as doxologia's and saint.gr's readings also left them. The Prologue prints no hymn.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru’s life936: «Праведная Глафира скончалась (+ 322), прежде чем приказ дошел до Амасии», and the day line heads her «(322)». The first year of any kind in this folder: doxologia, saint.gr and the Охридски пролог each give her none. No year of birth is given and none was inferred.
